Hi Meredith — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear highlights. Below are concise answers you can paste into the packet. I’ve kept them targeted to the hosted API offering and noted where Dedicated/Private differ.

1) Data residency / storage locations
- Primary storage: customer request/response payloads and metadata are stored in object storage within the AWS region selected at provisioning (we currently support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).
- Backups & snapshots: periodic encrypted backups of configuration/state are stored in the same region by default; cross-region replication is opt-in and requires explicit contractual agreement.
- Note: Model binaries and cache artifacts may be hosted in other regions for performance but do not contain customer request payloads.

2) Retention windows (hosted API default)
- Request/response data (raw payloads): default retention = 7 days. Customers can request shorter retention on onboarding.
- Request logs / telemetry (request ID, latency, status, routing): 30 days by default for debugging and billing; can be reduced to 14 days with an enterprise setting.
- Aggregated metrics and anonymized usage statistics: retained indefinitely for product analytics; no customer-identifying strings are kept in analytics buckets.
- Backups/snapshots: incremental snapshots retained for 90 days; full retention lifecycle is documented below.

3) Deletion / erasure process
- Customer-initiated erasure: we begin a deletion workflow within 24 hours of an approved request.
- Immediate actions: remove live objects from primary buckets and invalidate cache entries; purge associated ephemeral KV caches and logging indices referencing the customer.
- Snapshot/backups handling: backups are subject to snapshot lifecycle — we mark snapshots that contain the subject data for expedited removal and then run a secure expunge job to remove object versions (see attachment: data_purge_flow.png). Expected completion: up to 7 calendar days to remove data from live storage and object versions; up to 30 calendar days in cases where additional legal hold reviews are required.
- Verification: we provide a deletion certificate (hash of removed object keys and timestamps) on request.

4) What counts as customer data?
- Input prompts, model outputs, user-provided files, and any custom metadata you upload. System-level telemetry (sampling of prompt lengths, aggregate latency percentiles) is not considered customer data when stored in analytics buckets.

5) Backups & disaster recovery interplay
- Backup retention does not supersede immediate erasure. If a customer requests deletion, we perform targeted snapshot expunge operations. Where immutable backups are retained for DR, we track and prioritize removal or restricted access enforced by KMS key rotation policies.

6) Evidence and artifacts we can share
- Signed deletion certificate (PDF), audit logs showing the purge run, and a sanitized object-key export.

I’ve attached a compact CSV that maps our default retention settings for quick ingestion into procurement spreadsheets. If you need specific SLA language for contract clauses, Ben (cc’d) can add the legal/ops phrasing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call Monday AM PT.

Meredith — adding a few operational clarifications to Naomi’s summary (forwarded thread below).

- Deletion SLA: standard target = 7 business days for full expunge (live objects + object versions + index removal); 30 days max if legal or cross-team approvals required. We’ll commit to contract language if needed (we’ve done similar with other financial customers).
- Snapshots: incremental snapshots are stored as deltas; removal requires a compaction job and object version deletion — this is why snapshot expunge can take up to 7 business days in some cases.
- Cache artifacts: prefix/KV cache entries are ephemeral and garbage-collected within 24 hours after they are invalidated; they do not persist to backup unless configured for stateful workflows (this is relevant for FinSecure’s sync workflows).
- Access controls: deletion workflow is gated behind a two-person ops approval when executed outside the automated erasure flow (typically for legal holds).

I’ve attached a small diagram (data_purge_flow.png) that shows the steps our ops team runs when processing a full purge request. Happy to provide SLA wording for your procurement template.

-Ben
